title: Math Day at the Beach
text:
Math Day at the Beach is a mathematical problem solving festival for Southern California high school students, hosted by California State University, Long Beach (CSULB).

There is both individual and team competition. High schools can send one or two teams made of six members each, with about 34 teams in total. Before 2025, the competition took place on a Saturday in March. Since 2025, it has been on a Saturday in October. The questions are similar in difficulty to those of the AMC 12, spanning topics like algebra, geometry, probability, number theory, etc.

Format (Pre-2026)[edit]

The competition used to consist of two individual rounds, a team round, a relay round, and a faceoff round. The first individual round lasted 45 minutes and consisted of 15 multiple-choice questions, awarding 4 points for a correct answer, 1 point for a blank answer, and no points for an incorrect answer, for a maximum of 60 points. The second individual round was 25 minutes and consisted of 15 short free-response questions, with scoring being five times the number of correct answers, for a maximum of 25. The team round lasted for 30 minutes and consisted of 8 short free-response questions. The entire team worked together on this round, and submitted one set of answers. 10 points were awarded each correct answer, for a maximum of 80 points.

Format (2026)[edit]

For 2026, the individual rounds have been combined, as well as an optional tiebreaker question administered simultaneously with the individual round. The team round has been extended to 40 minutes and has twelve questions, with 10 points awarded for each correct answer. The relay round is unchanged, and the face-off round has been expanded to five contestants instead of four.

Individual Round - Part 1[edit]

This round lasts 30 minutes and consists of 6 five-option multiple-choice questions, six free-response questions, and one optional tiebreaker question. Scoring consists of:

  • 5 points for each correct free-response answer
  • 4 points for each correct multiple choice answer
  • 1 point for each blank answer
  • 0 points for each incorrect answer

This means that the maximum possible score is 54 points. Topics for individual-round questions may include algebra, geometry, trigonometry, logarithms, logic, elementary number theory, combinatorics, and probability, but will not involve calculus. Note that the tiebreaker question is only used to break ties and does not award points.

Team Round[edit]

This round lasts for 40 minutes and consists of 12 short-answer questions. The entire team works together on this round, submitting one set of answers. The team's score is 10 times the number of correct answers, for a maximum of 120 points. Typically, one or two questions on the team round require basic calculus.

Relay Round[edit]

This was introduced in 2008 and does not count towards teams' scores. It is similar in format to the ARML relay round. However, the top tree relay squads are given their own awards.

Faceoff Round[edit]

The top four individuals from the individual round meet in an oral round loosely modelled on the Mathcounts Countdown, but with longer time limits. Two competitors sit on the stage, and each is given a problem to work. The first to ring in is given a chance to say the correct answer; if that is wrong, the second person is given a limited amount of time (varying by question, usually 30 to 60 seconds) to ring in and answer. This is structured as a single-elimination tournament. In the first round, the winner is the first to answer two questions correctly; in the final round, the winner is the first to answer three questions correctly. The winner adds 10 points to his or her individual score (and his team's team score) and the 2nd place individual adds 5 points. While these point totals are relatively small, they have been decisive in determining individual and team winners in some years.

Tedrick Leung was the winner of the Faceoff Round for four consecutive years, 2004 through 2007.

Teacher Faceoff Round[edit]

Three teachers who volunteer will complete in a similar oral round for 15 minutes.
